title: Adaptive noise-fencing and reservation autocalibration for dedicated clusters
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: After the Feb capacity outage in cluster eu-west-2, the on-call postmortem identified three recurring contributors: undetected noisy tenants, conservative static reservations that left headroom unused, and an aggressive burst policy that amplified contention during spikes. This ticket proposes an end-to-end mitigation: a lightweight noise-fencing detector + per-tenant reservation autocalibration service that adjusts soft/guaranteed reservations on a short window, and a conservative burst throttling rewrite with circuit-breaker semantics. The goal is to reduce eviction storms, improve p95 tail latency for customers on Dedicated, and avoid capacity overcommit that harms SLOs.

Scope: prototype the detector and autocalibrator in staging, validate with replayed production traces, add observability and safety gates, land a gradual rollout on a small set of clusters, and bake an operational runbook. This is an engineering + SRE-led change requiring coordination with Console (alerts) and Runtime teams for kernel/batching interactions.
acceptance_criteria: Detector identifies >90% of noisy tenant episodes in curated spike trace set with <5% false positives
Autocalibrator reduces tenant-caused evictions by >=50% in replay tests compared to current reservations
New burst throttle prevents >80% of eviction cascades in chaos tests while preserving median latency within 10%
Telemetry dashboard surfaces per-tenant reservation changes, noise score, and rollback trigger counts
Runbook and automatic rollback API exist; rollout can be halted by on-call in <= 2 minutes
notes: Design constraints: must be cheap to run (no heavy ML model), operate with the existing allocation service API, and respect tenant-level billing/quotas. Trade-offs: shorter calibration windows react faster but risk oscillation; we'll use hysteresis and weighted EMA to stabilize. We will prefer soft reservation increases over hard guaranteed changes to avoid billing implications. For noisy detection we use a composite signal (token-per-second spike + KV cache miss spikes + sustained GPU memory pressure) instead of single metric detection.
implementation_plan: 1) Build a streaming detector that ingests tenant-level telemetry (rps, tokens/sec, kv-cache-hit-rate, eviction-count) into a windowed scorer; 2) Prototype autocalibrator that proposes soft reservation diffs and applies them via the existing reservation API with a 10-minute dry-run and revert if tail-latency regresses; 3) Implement burst-policy rewrite: token-bucket per-tenant with adaptive refill and circuit-breaker that trips on concurrent eviction rate; 4) Add dashboards and SLO-based rollout gates; 5) Run replay tests on staging traces and a 2-cluster canary; 6) Gradual rollout with 24h observation, then expand.
rollback_plan: Expose a single feature-flag per-cluster. Immediate rollback: disable autocalibrator and revert to last saved reservation snapshot. Emergency kill-switch: cluster-level throttle set to conservative defaults. On-call runbook includes commands to list recent reservation deltas, block a tenant, and revert via CLI. Expected rollback latency: <2 minutes for feature flag change, <10 minutes to revert state if needed.
testing_plan: Unit tests for scorer logic, integration test with allocation API mocks, replay-based validation with 3 months of anonymized production traces, chaos injected tests (delay and eviction injection), and a 2-week canary collecting p50/p95/p99 latency, eviction counts, and cost delta. Ensure synthetic noisy tenants are included to validate detection thresholds.
estimated_cost_impact: expected small increase in average reserved capacity (<3%) while reducing eviction-induced SLO violations
